declaration.negotiation_history_statement: I submit this statement in support of preliminary approval under Rule 23(e). The parties negotiated both class relief and attorneys’ fees from the first round; fees were not deferred until after class relief was agreed. Class counsel initially proposed a $32 million class fund and $7 million in fees and expenses. Brightline countered with a $28 million fund and up to $6 million in fees and expenses. Class counsel then proposed a $32 million fund and up to $5 million in fees and expenses, which Brightline accepted. Throughout the exchange, both sides proposed automatic distribution to identified class members, independent court review of fees, no clear-sailing provision, and payment of any unawarded fees to the class rather than Brightline. The resulting agreement provides automatic payments without a claims process. The $32 million fund represents half of the $64 million in disputed charges and provides a certain recovery despite unresolved class-certification and trial risks and the time litigation would require. Fees are paid separately from the fund and remain subject to court approval. I believe the settlement warrants preliminary approval and notice to the class.

backchannel.speaker: plaintiff
backchannel.message: Our priority is meaningful, automatic payments to all identifiable members, without unclaimed funds reverting to Brightline. Any fee request must be reasonable, separately reviewed by the court, and structured so any reduction benefits the class. We are open to discussing a prompt resolution on that basis.

backchannel.speaker: defense
backchannel.message: We hear you on automatic payments and avoiding reversion. We’re prepared to discuss a structure with direct payments to identified members, court-reviewed fees, and any fee reduction going to the class. If we can agree on an overall amount that reflects the risks and avoids further delay, there may be a prompt path to resolution.

backchannel.speaker: plaintiff
backchannel.message: We could move promptly on a $34 million class fund, distributed automatically to identified members, plus $6 million in court-reviewed fees and expenses. Any fee reduction would go to the class, not Brightline. If that total is outside your range, please tell us what class fund Brightline can support while preserving those distribution protections.

backchannel.speaker: defense
backchannel.message: We can preserve automatic payments to identified members, with any court-reduced fees going to the class. A $34 million fund plus $6 million in fees is difficult for Brightline.
